newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers seek NRC reactor watchlist review.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers seek NRC reactor watchlist review.

text.p: Two Massachusetts lawmakers asked the General Accounting Office to check the adequacy and completeness of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's watch list of nuclear plants with safety or operational problems.

"...recent events have called into question the adequacy of the process through which nuclear power plants are named to the watch list as well as the NRC staff's oversight of plants named to the list," Sen. John Kerry and Rep. Edward Markey, both Democrats, said in a letter to Comptroller General Charles Bowsher.

"In addition, the NRC appears to have allowed problem nuclear power plants to continue to operate despite the fact that they appear to have failed to significantly improve their safety performance," the lawmakers' letter said.

The lawmakers said they wanted to know why Northeast Utilities' Millstone plant in Haddam Neck, Connecticut, was not named to the watch list until January 1996, and was named "only after national media attention began to focus on the very serious safety problems that have plagued the Millstone reactors."
They also said "significant safety questions" have been raised about other reactors in New England that were not on the NRC watch list.
The consumer group Public Citizen last week issued a list of 25 nuclear reactors across the country that it deemed the worst, which included four in New England.
The Massachusetts lawakers asked the GAO, Congress' investigative agency, to compare safety criteria used by Public Citizen and by the NRC staff.
